title: Bitwarden desktop app data
whyItMatters: The Bitwarden desktop app keeps an encrypted vault, account state and logs here. The folder shows a password manager was used on this computer and how much vault data was kept.
source: Bitwarden Help, Data Storage: Linux standard installs at ~/.config/Bitwarden - https://bitwarden.com/help/data-storage/
notes: Flatpak uses ~/.var/app/com.bitwarden.desktop and Snap uses ~/snap/bitwarden/current/.config/Bitwarden. Vault data is encrypted; nothing is opened or decrypted.

cleanup.exportFirst: Open Bitwarden and export a copy of every vault you need, then check that the exported file opens before removing anything.
cleanup.signOut: Sign out of Bitwarden on this computer, then in the web vault deauthorize this device's session so the account no longer trusts it.
steps: Confirm the vault export opens and you know the master password.
Sign out of Bitwarden and deauthorize this device in the web vault.
If you decide to remove the app, uninstall Bitwarden from your software manager or Flatpak.
Delete the Bitwarden folder named in the plan only after the export is confirmed.
cleanup.risk: Removes the encrypted vault and settings from this computer. Without a working export or account access, the vault items here cannot be recovered.
